title: Sandpiper — Acadia Health implementation scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for Acadia Health private deployment (notes to self).

Context: Acadia is a regional healthcare provider. They require private control plane, HSM-backed key management, strict egress policy, and model pinning for audits. They plan to run Redwood Private in their AWS account (gov-cloud-ish pattern) with a dedicated pool for clinical summarization routes.

Daily goals (short):
- Finalize VPC peer topology with infra (Miguel) — need peering CIDR map.
- Confirm KMS HSM integration approach with security (Hannah).
- Draft canary rollout plan for patient_summary route (small subset of docs).
- Run baseline perf test with 6.7B quant pipeline and 1024 token window.

Open questions / blockers:
- KMS: customer insists on HSM (CloudHSM). Does Redwood Private support CloudHSM via BYOK? We can map to KMS key wrapped with HSM but need legal signoff. (askSecurity)
- Egress: Acadia disallows internet egress from inference hosts. Need to confirm allowed registries for model artifacts and image pull strategy.
- Log retention: they want 2y audit logs for access. Storage plan/cost TBD.
- Throughput SLO: target <120ms p50 for patient_summary (200–400 token avg). Need perf verification.

Implementation checklist (working):
- [ ] Network: diagram + terraform blocks for VPC peering and route tables.
- [ ] IAM: cross-account role to allow Redwood operator to provision roles in customer account (least-priv).
- [ ] KMS: test encrypt/decrypt with customer key; get key arn.
- [ ] Images: build-private-registry pipeline or establish ECR read access from cluster nodes.
- [ ] Model pinning: pick model v1.2.1 (quantized) and record sha256.
- [ ] Canary plan: sample 1% traffic first 24h, 5% next 24h, rollback thresholds.
- [ ] E2E perf run: 50 qps sustained for 30m, capture p50/p90/p99 and token cost.
- [ ] Runbook: incident steps (fallback to hosted small model variant).

Notes / quick configs:
- Intended model: rwi-clinical-6.7b-q8a v1.2.1 (quantized). Lockfile: model_sha=5e3b7f9d
- Default route config (pseudo):
  route: /patient_summary
  model: rwi-clinical-6.7b-q8a
  batch: auto (target latency 120ms p50)
  prefix_cache: enabled (cache keys: patient_id, template_version)

Terraform sketch (for infra team):
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "acadia_redwood" {
  vpc_id = var.acadia_vpc_id
  peer_vpc_id = var.redwood_ops_vpc
  tags = { Name = "acadia-rw-peering" }
}
```
(put in acadia-infra repo, separate PR)

Quick perf commands (local):
- rwctl perf --target https://acadia-api.redwood.local/patient_summary --qps 50 --duration 30m --payload sample_patient_512.json
- collect logs: kubectl logs -l app=redwood-inference --since=1h > ~/acadia/perf/2025-11-03.log

Canary rollout notes:
- Canary buckets: 0.5%, 1%, 5%
- Observability: wire up per-route latency alert: alert if p95 > 300ms for 10m OR error_rate > 0.5%
- Automatic fallback: route to rwi-clinical-6.7b-q8a-lite if token errors > 0.1%

Customer-specific config gotchas I ran into yesterday:
- Acadia uses a strict proxy that mutates TLS SNI; image pulls failed until we set ECR endpoint in allowed list.
- Their secure dev account blocked CloudFormation stacks that create IAM roles with wildcard trusts; needed explicit ARNs.

Meeting takeaways (11/04 sync with Acadia infra):
- They will provide KMS key arn by EOD Friday.
- Provide explicit IAM trust ARNs in next terraform diff.
- They asked for an offline demo (screencast) that shows canary rollback (make short 6–8 minute video).

Short-term action items (assigned):
- Miguel: draft vpc/route terraform (due 11/07).
- Hannah: KMS integration note + security checklist (due 11/05).
- Me (Riya): build perf harness + baseline numbers; produce canary playbook + demo video (due 11/10).

Perf baseline (initial run notes):
- Setup: 3-node GPU pool (A100-like), model quantized q8a, batch target default 8.
- Observed: p50 ~ 140ms, p90 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 760ms at 50 qps (512 token average).
- Memory: roughly 14GB GPU mem free under this config with kv cache warmed.
- Action: increase batch timeout tuning -> try batch target 6 and reserved slots 2.

Runbook excerpt (to refine):
- Detect: route p95 > 350ms OR error_rate spike -> page SE oncall.
- Quick mitigation: 1) Increase replicas by +1 (if capacity), 2) Lower model to lite variant, 3) Enable synchronous fallback to hosted endpoint (if allowed by contract).
- Post-mortem: gather token traces and last 1h of model logs, export to secure S3 bucket.

Notes to self (random):
- Remember to capture model sha and put in audit doc before handing to compliance.
- Screen-record the canary rollback exercise. Tiny script:
  export DEMO_KEY=<temp>
  ./scripts/run_canary_demo.sh --route patient_summary --duration 600

Fragments / scratch thoughts:
- Might recommend quant-ptq + small per-token-cost savings vs q8a (need eval).
- Consider prefix-only caching for repeat discharge-summary templates (huge win).
- If they insist on zero internet egress for proxies, we may need to mirror base images in their ECR and run full air-gapped deploy flow.

References / links to copy into formal PR: Confluence onboarding page (linked), internal perf dashboard (TBD), acadia-jira epic JIRA-ACAD-212.

-- end scratchpad (will move items into formal PR and runbook once baselines are solid).
